chunks: Al-Barqi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Hilal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about two men who killed each other while they were in the state of Ihram, so he said, 'Glory be to Allah, what a bad thing they did.' I said, 'But they have done it, so what is obligatory upon them?' He said, 'Upon each one of them is the blood-money (diya).'

key_terms.مُحْرِمَانِ: Two men in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for two pilgrims who kill each other while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when two pilgrims in Ihram kill each other, the liability for blood-money (diya) is individual rather than collective, with each paying for the other. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between intentional homicide and the specific penalties incurred during the sacred state of Ihram, emphasizing personal accountability for the violation of pilgrimage sanctity.
